description: System modules hardening: config persistence, contextual audit trail, Prometheus UsageCollector metrics, path-filter reload, and startup failure handling. Closes Issue #45.

test_cases.description: update_config with overrides_path configured writes the change to the YAML overrides file
When overrides.yaml exists on startup, its values are applied after the base config
update_config call with context.identity set produces an audit entry with actor_id from context.identity.id
toggle_feature call produces an audit entry with before/after values in the change field
When Prometheus is enabled and UsageCollector has call data, GET /metrics includes apcore_usage_calls_total
reload_module with path_filter 'executor.*' reloads all modules matching the pattern in dependency topological order
Providing both module_id and path_filter to reload_module raises MODULE_RELOAD_CONFLICT
When fail_on_error=True and a system module registration fails, register_sys_modules raises SysModuleRegistrationError immediately
When fail_on_error=False (default) and a system module registration fails, register_sys_modules logs at ERROR level and continues

Rust register_sys_modules returns Result<SysModulesContext, SysModuleError> — Ok(SysModulesContext) on success, Err(SysModuleError) on failure. The Ok arm carries the registered-module map and the shared EventEmitter/ToggleState/ErrorHistory/UsageCollector handles, matching apcore-python's returned context dict; it is NOT unit.

Bulk reload MUST order by the declared dependency graph, and the only way to observe that is a graph whose topological order DISAGREES with the alphabet. `executor.alpha` depends on `executor.zulu`, so the dependency order is zulu-then-alpha while a plain sort yields alpha-then-zulu. `reload_with_path_filter` cannot discriminate — its three modules declare no dependencies on each other, so every permutation is a valid topological order and an assertion there passes whatever the SDK does. Both apcore-python and apcore-typescript degenerated to alphabetical for the same underlying reason (the metadata merge dropped `dependencies` before the post-registration accessor could see it) and each fixed it with a repo-local test; nothing proved the three agree. See apcore-typescript#35.

D-110: with no `project.name` configured, `system.manifest.full` reports project_name `"apcore"`. Two SDKs reported `""` while their own `system.health.summary` already reported `"apcore"` — the decision was taken on internal consistency rather than an SDK majority, so the paired case below is part of it, not a nicety.

D-110, the other half. In the SAME configuration `system.health.summary` reports the same project_name. A case pinning only `manifest.full` would leave the contradiction the decision removed unpinned — an SDK could satisfy it and still have its two system modules disagree.

D-119: every registered `system.*` module DECLARES `open_world: false` — no system module reaches an external system. The second half of the decision is that it is written out rather than inherited: the language default is `true`, which means the opposite of the intended value, and that is how the divergence arose. So the assertion reads the module's DECLARED annotations rather than an effective value computed with defaults applied. The read is get_definition().annotations rather than any per-language class attribute: that is the surface system.manifest.* publishes, so it is what a consumer actually sees, and it is the one shape all three SDKs share.

D-109: `error_rate_threshold` moves the HEALTHY/DEGRADED boundary only. The degraded/error boundary is the classification table's fixed 0.10.

The discriminating input is a threshold of 0.001 with an observed error rate of 0.05. An SDK computing the second boundary as `threshold * 10` puts it at 0.01 and answers `error`; the table answers `degraded`. apcore-python and apcore-typescript both scaled it, so a module erroring 5% of the time was `error` there and `degraded` on apcore-rust — for the same module, the same metrics and the same configuration.

The consequence is recorded because it surprises: at 0.001, `degraded` spans 0.1%-10%. A caller wanting a stricter ERROR boundary is asking for a second knob that deliberately does not exist.

D-109 control. The SAME threshold of 0.001 with an error rate of 0.5 MUST be `error`.

Without it, 'not scaled' is also satisfied by an implementation that removed the error boundary altogether and classified everything above the healthy threshold as `degraded`. This pins the boundary AT the table's 0.10 rather than merely establishing that it does not move with the input.

driver_contract.ordering_needs_a_disagreeing_graph: Assert `reload_order_observed` as an ORDERED list against the sequence the SDK actually reloaded in — the unregister/register calls, not a field in the response. A driver that reads back a report is asserting a relabelling, not the order work happened in. `alphabetical_order_would_be` is stated so a driver can show the two differ; a case where they coincide proves nothing, which is exactly the state `reload_with_path_filter` is in.
driver_contract.dependencies_must_survive_registration: The dependency must be declared through the SAME path an application uses, and read back through the post-registration accessor. Both SDKs that had this bug lost `dependencies` in the metadata merge while discovery-time sorting kept working — so a driver that supplies the graph directly to the sort would pass against an implementation whose accessor returns nothing.
